RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Sawyer Iverson
Member ID: W437498644
Reference/Tracking Number: POC-C1EE0F5DA7-11270
Date of Notice: 2026-08-10
Service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296
Requesting/Operating Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (bunion surgery/hallux valgus correction), noticed to me on 2026-08-10. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I disagree with this determination and am submitting this appeal, along with the clinical records summarized below, within the 180-day window your plan allows. I note that your own member grievance and appeal form states: "This form must be filed within 180 days of an adverse determination," and this appeal is being submitted well within that period.

Preliminary request regarding applicable criteria: The denial notice does not cite a specific medical policy number, title, or set of clinical criteria. I have reviewed Ambetter of Tennessee's published Clinical & Payment Policies list and did not find a plan-specific policy addressing bunionectomy or hallux valgus correction. That same source states that "Ambetter of Tennessee utilizes InterQual® criteria for those medical technologies, procedures or pharmaceutical treatments for which a Ambetter of Tennessee clinical policy does not exist." Because I have not been given the text of the specific InterQual criteria (or any other clinical criteria) that were applied to my request, I am not able to quote or respond to that language directly, and I want to be explicit that nothing below is a quotation of Ambetter's or InterQual's medical-necessity standard. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Ambetter of Tennessee provide me and Dr. Reyes with a copy of the specific criteria (InterQual SmartSheet or otherwise) and the reviewer's written rationale used to deny this request, so that we may respond to the precise standard being applied.

In the absence of that document, I am submitting the clinical documentation below because it addresses the elements that are generally required to support medical necessity for surgical correction of hallux valgus, and I believe it demonstrates that my request was supported by complete, not incomplete, documentation:

1. Duration and severity of symptoms: I have had 12 months of progressive foot pain that has not been relieved by rest.

2. Conservative (non-surgical) treatment trial: I completed a structured course of conservative care from 2026-03-20 to 2026-07-10 (16 weeks, 20 visits), including activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, a copy of which is enclosed [attach PT discharge note].

3. Medication trial: I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-25 that provided only 2 weeks of partial relief. [Attach medication/injection records.]

4. Objective imaging findings: Weight-bearing radiographs of the foot obtained on 2026-06-29 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. [Attach imaging report and films.]

5. Functional impairment: I am unable to tolerate closed shoes, and there is a documented risk of skin ulceration over the bony prominence.

6. Physical examination findings: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. [Attach exam note.]

7. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29.

This clinical picture — 12 months of unrelieved pain, a completed and well-documented 16-week course of orthotic/shoewear/activity modification with 20 visits, 8 months of NSAID therapy plus a corticosteroid injection with only transient partial relief, objective radiographic deformity (38° HVA / 17° IMA), and functional/skin-integrity risk — reflects a complete conservative-treatment and diagnostic workup, not an incomplete one. If any specific document, measurement, or note was missing from the file reviewed by Ambetter's medical director, I ask that this be identified specifically so that Dr. Reyes's office can supply it; to date, I have not been told which document(s) were considered incomplete.

Enclosed with this appeal are the following records supporting medical necessity:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-20 to 2026-07-10)
- Medication and corticosteroid injection records (NSAID trial; injection dated 2026-05-25)
- Weight-bearing foot radiograph report dated 2026-06-29
- Office visit/exam note documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Surgeon's (Dr. Reyes) letter of medical necessity
- [Any additional records not listed above]

I respectfully request that Ambetter of Tennessee:
1. Overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 28296; or
2. If the plan maintains that documentation remains incomplete, identify in writing the specific missing item(s) so they can be promptly supplied; and
3. Provide, in writing, the specific medical policy or InterQual criteria applied to this request, consistent with my right to understand the basis for this adverse determination.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address and phone number above, with a copy to Dr. Reyes's office at [surgeon office fax/address]. I understand I have the right to have this appeal considered under the plan's internal appeal process and, if unsuccessful, to request an independent external review.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Iverson
Member ID: W437498644
